pure-announcement.rationale: This is an educational survey of a technique with a traced research lineage (ReAct, Reflexion, evaluator-optimizer, orchestrator-workers), not a launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: No existing concept covers loop engineering; context-layer (a company-brain context system) and agent-skills-format (the SKILL.md packaging format) are cited only as building blocks the loop reaches for, and a reader of neither learns this material there.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Central claims are anchored to primary sources — arXiv papers for ReAct and Reflexion, Anthropic's engineering guides, the LangChain and Osmani essays, and dated primary posts — that a reader can check.

durability.rationale: The substance is mechanisms, patterns, and trade-offs (the reason-act-observe loop, layered termination exits, deterministic-over-model verification, hill-climbing on traces) that age well; the June-2026 timeline and view counts are incidental color, not the load-bearing content.

actionability.rationale: It changes how a reader builds — start with one goal, one deterministic verifier, a hard iteration cap and one escalation path on a low-stakes recurring task before stacking loops — and gives concrete design decisions (what counts as verifier.passes, how compact and no_progress behave) plus a pattern-selection guide.

atomicity.rationale: The note is a comprehensive survey bundling several standalone concepts — the prompt/context/harness/loop layer progression, the anatomy-plus-pseudocode of a reliable loop, the four stacked loops (agent/verification/event-driven/hill-climbing), the loop-pattern taxonomy, and the three hard problems (context/termination/verification) — each of which could be its own concept, so the split is the finding.
